questions.question: Which of the following movements of Mahatma Gandhi was his first movement in British India against indigo planters?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Champaran Satyagraha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Champaran Satyagraha (1917)** was Mahatma Gandhi's first civil disobedience movement in British India against indigo planters.
 
• It was initiated after farmers in Champaran, Bihar, were forced to cultivate indigo under the oppressive **tinkathia system** by British landlords.
 
• Gandhi's involvement was prompted by a request from local farmer **Raj Kumar Shukla**, who highlighted the plight of indigo farmers.
 
• The movement marked Gandhi's transition into Indian politics and his experimental application of satyagraha principles in the country.
 
• The success of Champaran Satyagraha led to the abolition of the tinkathia system and paved the way for further movements against colonial exploitation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tinkathia System:**

 
 
• Under this system, farmers were forced to dedicate 3/20th of their land to indigo cultivation without adequate compensation.
 
• The system caused severe economic hardship and environmental degradation for farmers.
 
 
 
• **Satyagraha:**
 
 
• A principle of nonviolent resistance developed by Gandhi to fight injustice.
 
• It emphasizes truth, nonviolence, and peaceful protest as tools to achieve social change.
 
 
 
• **Raj Kumar Shukla:**
 
 
• A farmer from Champaran who played a pivotal role in bringing Gandhi to Bihar to address the plight of indigo farmers.
 
• He is considered a key figure in the initiation of the Champaran Satyagraha.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Champaran Satyagraha:**
 
 
• The movement successfully pressured the British administration to form an inquiry committee to address farmers' grievances.
 
• It marked the first victory of satyagraha in India and established Gandhi's leadership in the national independence struggle.

questions.question: Which of the following is the regulatory body for microfinance institutions in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reserve Bank of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** is the primary regulatory authority for microfinance institutions (MFIs) in India.
 
• RBI regulates MFIs under its **Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC)-Microfinance Institutions** framework.
 
• The RBI has established specific guidelines for NBFC-MFIs, including norms for **lending practices, interest rates, and customer protection**.
 
• Microfinance institutions play a vital role in providing financial services to **low-income groups and underserved populations**, and RBI ensures these operations adhere to ethical and sustainable practices.
 
• RBI periodically reviews and updates regulations for MFIs to ensure a **balanced growth of the microfinance sector** while safeguarding borrower interests.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Microfinance:**

 
 
• Refers to **financial services such as loans, savings, and insurance** provided to low-income individuals or groups who lack access to traditional banking services.
 
• It aims to **empower economically disadvantaged populations** and promote financial inclusion.
 
• Microfinance institutions primarily focus on small loans, often without collateral, to support entrepreneurial ventures.
 
 
 
• **NBFC-MFI:**
 
 
• Non-Banking Financial Companies categorized as Microfinance Institutions (NBFC-MFI) are regulated by the RBI.
 
• To qualify as an NBFC-MFI, at least **85% of the assets** must be in the form of microfinance loans.
 
• Interest rates charged by NBFC-MFIs are capped by the RBI to ensure affordability for borrowers.
 
 
 
• **Priority Sector Lending (PSL):**
 
 
• Microfinance falls under the **Priority Sector Lending** category, where banks are mandated by RBI to lend a certain proportion of their funds to priority sectors.
 
• This ensures that credit is made available to marginalized sectors, including agriculture, micro-enterprises, and low-income groups.
 
 
 
• **Key RBI Regulations for MFIs:**
 
 
• RBI mandates MFIs to follow a **fair lending code** to ensure borrower protection.
 
• MFIs must adhere to a **loan size limit** and interest rate caps as prescribed by RBI.
 
• Periodic reporting and audits are conducted by RBI to ensure compliance and transparency in operations.

questions.question: The tableau of which of the following states showcased the resistance of indigenous people towards the British Imperial Policy during the Republic Day Parade of 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arunachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The tableau of **Arunachal Pradesh** during the Republic Day Parade 2022 depicted the resistance of indigenous people against the British Imperial policies.
 
• The theme of the tableau highlighted the contribution of **freedom fighters like Matmur Jamoh**, a prominent figure in Arunachal's resistance.
 
• It showcased the historic **Anglo-Abor Wars**, which were pivotal in resisting British intrusion in the tribal areas of Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• The tableau emphasized **indigenous culture**, bravery, and the spirit of resistance of the local tribes against colonial oppression.
 
• Arunachal Pradesh's tableau was one of several state displays that reflected India's rich history and cultural diversity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Matmur Jamoh**

 
 
• He was an important tribal leader who led the resistance against British forces in Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• In 1911, Jamoh and his followers killed a British officer, Noel Williamson, in protest against colonial exploitation.
 
• He was later captured and sent to the infamous Cellular Jail in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
 
 
 
• **Anglo-Abor Wars**
 
 
• These were a series of conflicts between the British and the Abor tribes of Arunachal Pradesh during the 19th and early 20th centuries.
 
• The wars were primarily fought over British attempts to control the region and impose their policies.
 
• The resistance showcased the bravery and independence of the tribal communities.
 
 
 
• **Republic Day Parade**
 
 
• The parade is held annually on January 26th to celebrate the adoption of the Indian Constitution in 1950.
 
• It features tableaux from various states and union territories, showcasing their culture, achievements, and history.
 
• The event also includes performances by military and cultural groups, reflecting India's unity in diversity.
 
 
 
• **Indigenous Resistance in India**
 
 
• Several indigenous communities across India resisted British colonial rule, including the Santhal, Munda, and Gond uprisings.
 
• These movements were often rooted in protecting land rights, cultural identity, and traditional governance systems.
 
• The stories of such resistance highlight the broader struggle for India's independence.

questions.question: Gopi Krishna, a great personality in Kathak and famous as an Indian dancer, actor and choreographer belong to which gharana?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Banaras**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Gopi Krishna** was a renowned exponent of Kathak dance and is celebrated as a dancer, actor, and choreographer.
 
• He belonged to the **Banaras Gharana**, one of the prominent schools of Kathak known for its distinct style and techniques.
 
• Gopi Krishna is widely recognized for his exceptional speed, rhythm, and creative choreography in Kathak.
 
• He played a pivotal role in popularizing Kathak both within India and internationally through performances and films.
 
• Banaras Gharana emphasizes subtle expressions, intricate rhythmic patterns, and graceful movements, characteristics often associated with Gopi Krishna’s style.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathak**

 
 
• Kathak is one of the eight classical dance forms of India and has its roots in the storytelling traditions of North India.
 
• The term "Kathak" is derived from the Sanskrit word "Katha," meaning story, and "Kathakar," meaning storyteller.
 
• This dance form is characterized by intricate footwork, spins, facial expressions, and gestures.
 
• Kathak has three major gharanas or schools: Lucknow, Jaipur, and Banaras, each with its unique style.
 
 
 
• **Banaras Gharana**
 
 
• It is one of the key gharanas of Kathak, originating in Varanasi (Banaras), Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The style is known for its fluid movements, emphasis on expressiveness (abhinaya), and use of intricate rhythmic patterns.
 
• Banaras Gharana incorporates elements of spirituality and storytelling, often focusing on mythological themes.
 
 
 
• **Gopi Krishna in Cinema**
 
 
• He contributed to Indian cinema by choreographing and performing dance sequences in various films.
 
• Notable movies featuring his work include "Jhanak Jhanak Payal Baaje," where his dance gained widespread acclaim.
 
 
 
• **Other Prominent Kathak Gharanas**
 
 
• **Lucknow Gharana:** Known for its grace, elegance, and emphasis on facial expressions.
 
• **Jaipur Gharana:** Focuses on powerful footwork, intricate patterns, and vigorous movements.
 
• **Raigarh Gharana:** A comparatively modern gharana that blends elements from other schools and emphasizes innovation.

questions.question: As per 2018, what is the number of mobile subscribers per 100 people in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**87**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per 2018 statistics, India had approximately **87 mobile subscribers per 100 people**, reflecting high mobile penetration in the country.
 
• The telecom sector in India experienced rapid growth due to **affordable plans, increased smartphone usage, and 4G network expansion**.
 
• India became the **second-largest telecom market globally** in terms of the number of subscribers, with mobile connectivity reaching rural and urban areas alike.
 
• The growth was fueled by major operators like **Reliance Jio, Airtel, and Vodafone Idea**, who contributed significantly to the increase in subscription rates.
 
• As of 2018, the Indian telecom sector had over **1.2 billion mobile subscribers**, showcasing its importance in the global telecom landscape.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Telecom Density**

 
 
• Telecom density (Teledensity) measures the number of telephone connections (mobile and landline) for every 100 individuals in a region.
 
• India's teledensity has been steadily increasing, driven by affordable mobile services and rural network expansion.
 
 
 
• **Urban vs Rural Subscribers**
 
 
• Urban areas contribute significantly to mobile subscriber numbers, but growth in rural areas surged due to government initiatives and operator incentives.
 
• In 2018, urban teledensity stood at around **156.9%**, while rural teledensity was approximately **59.5%**.
 
 
 
• **Role of Digital India Initiative**
 
 
• The Indian government’s **Digital India program** aimed to enhance connectivity and promote digital inclusion across the country.
 
• Efforts like broadband penetration and affordable mobile data plans accelerated the adoption of mobile services.
 
 
 
• **Global Comparison**
 
 
• India ranks high globally in terms of the sheer number of mobile subscribers but faces challenges like **network congestion** and uneven quality of service.
 
• As of 2018, countries like the USA and Japan had higher mobile penetration rates, but India's growth trajectory is notable.

questions.question: Who is known as the father of Indian Census?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Henry Walter**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Henry Walter** is regarded as the "Father of the Indian Census" for organizing the first modern census in India in 1830.
 
• The first systematic census in India was conducted under British rule by Henry Walter in the town of Dacca (now Dhaka) in 1830.
 
• Henry Walter was instrumental in introducing the concept of recording population statistics in an organized and structured manner.
 
• This laid the foundation for the decennial census system in India, which officially began in 1872 and continues to this day.
 
• The census in India now provides critical data for planning and policy-making, a practice rooted in the groundwork laid by Henry Walter.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Census Overview:**

 
 
• The Indian Census is conducted every 10 years, providing detailed demographic, social, and economic data.
 
• The first official synchronous census in India was conducted in 1881 under British rule.
 
• Post-independence, the Census of India is conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
 
 
• **Decennial Census:**
 
 
• The census collects data on population, literacy, occupation, religion, language, and housing, among other parameters.
 
• The data is vital for planning welfare schemes, resource allocation, and policy formulation.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Census:**
 
 
• It helps in understanding the demographic changes and trends over time.
 
• The census data is crucial for electoral delimitation and the allocation of parliamentary seats.
 
• It supports the government in addressing socio-economic issues effectively.
 
 
 
• **Modern Census Techniques:**
 
 
• The 2021 Census aimed to leverage digital technologies for faster and more accurate data collection.
 
• For the first time, citizens were given the option of self-enumeration through a mobile app.

questions.question: During whose reign was Devagiri renamed Daulatabad?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Devagiri, a city in Maharashtra, was renamed Daulatabad by Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq during his reign in the 14th century.
 
• In 1327, Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq ordered the transfer of his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad as part of his administrative reforms.
 
• Daulatabad was chosen for its central location in India, which was considered ideal for controlling the entire kingdom.
 
• The decision to shift the capital was controversial and led to significant hardships for the population, as many were forced to migrate.
 
• Eventually, Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq reversed the decision and moved the capital back to Delhi, citing logistical and administrative challenges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq:**

 
 
• Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq was the second ruler of the Tughlaq dynasty and reigned from 1325 to 1351.
 
• He is known for his ambitious and often controversial policies, such as the introduction of token currency and shifting the capital to Daulatabad.
 
• His reign is marked by both administrative innovation and widespread discontent due to failed experiments.
 
 
 
• **Devagiri:**
 
 
• Devagiri was originally a fortified city under the Yadava dynasty before being annexed by the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• It was strategically located in the Deccan region, making it an important center for trade and administration.
 
 
 
• **Capital Shift to Daulatabad:**
 
 
• This policy aimed to consolidate the Sultanate's control over the Deccan and create a more centralized administration.
 
• The forced migration led to immense suffering for the people and logistical failures, making it one of the most debated decisions of his reign.
 
 
 
• **Tughlaq Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Tughlaq dynasty ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1320 to 1414.
 
• It is known for its architectural contributions and administrative innovations, despite facing frequent rebellions.

questions.question: What is e-Sawaari that was launched by Niti Ayog in December 2021 in partnership with Convergence Energy Service Limited (CESL) and World Resources Institute, India (WRI India), and supported by Transformative Urban Mobility Initiative (TUMI)?

options.text: Portal for all information on electric vehicles
Mobile app for state run buses and Indian railways
Scheme for 100% electrification of broad gauge railway routes across India
Electric Bus Coalition for Accelerating deployment of e-buses in India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electric Bus Coalition for Accelerating deployment of e-buses in India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **e-Sawaari** is an Electric Bus Coalition launched by Niti Ayog in December 2021 in collaboration with CESL and WRI India.
 
• The initiative aims to accelerate the deployment of electric buses (e-buses) across India to promote sustainable urban mobility.
 
• The coalition provides a platform for stakeholders, including government agencies, bus operators, and financiers, to share knowledge and best practices regarding e-bus adoption.
 
• This program is supported by the **Transformative Urban Mobility Initiative (TUMI)**, which focuses on improving urban mobility and reducing carbon emissions globally.
 
• It seeks to address challenges such as financing, operational efficiency, and infrastructure development for electric buses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electric Buses:**

 
 
• Electric buses are an eco-friendly alternative to traditional diesel-powered buses, reducing greenhouse gas emissions and air pollution.
 
• They use electric motors powered by batteries and are considered crucial for sustainable urban transport.
 
• India’s push for electric buses aligns with its commitment to achieving net-zero emissions by 2070.
 
 
 
• **Convergence Energy Services Limited (CESL):**
 
 
• CESL is a subsidiary of Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL), focusing on clean energy projects and sustainable development.
 
• It plays a key role in managing and implementing initiatives like e-Sawaari.
 
 
 
• **World Resources Institute (WRI India):**
 
 
• WRI India is a research organization that works on sustainable development, with a focus on urban mobility, climate, and energy.
 
• It collaborates with governments and stakeholders to support initiatives like e-Sawaari.
 
 
 
• **Transformative Urban Mobility Initiative (TUMI):**
 
 
• TUMI is a global initiative led by Germany to promote sustainable urban mobility in developing countries.
 
• It supports the development of electric mobility solutions, including e-buses, to combat climate change.

questions.question: Henry Vivian Derozio is related to which of the following movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Young Bengal Movement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Henry Vivian Derozio was a prominent social reformer and teacher in early 19th century Bengal, associated with the **Young Bengal Movement**.
 
• The Young Bengal Movement was characterized by its advocacy for **rationalism, liberty, equality, and freedom of thought**.
 
• Derozio instilled progressive ideas among his students at Hindu College, Calcutta, encouraging them to question societal norms and practices.
 
• He and his followers were influenced by the ideals of the **French Revolution** and sought to promote scientific thinking and secularism.
 
• The movement played a significant role in the **Bengal Renaissance**, laying the groundwork for future social reform initiatives in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Young Bengal Movement:**

 
 
• It emerged in Bengal during the 1820s and 1830s under the leadership of Henry Vivian Derozio.
 
• The followers of Derozio were called "Derozians," and they aimed to reform Indian society by promoting **modern education and critical thinking**.
 
• The movement emphasized the importance of **abolishing superstitions and social evils**, such as caste discrimination and sati.
 
 
 
• **Bengal Renaissance:**
 
 
• The Bengal Renaissance was a period of **cultural, social, and intellectual awakening** in Bengal during the 19th and early 20th centuries.
 
• It included contributions from reformers like Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, and Derozio.
 
• The Renaissance fostered a shift from traditional practices to modern ideas of equality, education, and rationalism.
 
 
 
• **Henry Vivian Derozio:**
 
 
• Derozio was born in 1809 and was of Portuguese descent; he is considered one of the earliest **Indian advocates of liberalism**.
 
• He taught at Hindu College, where he inspired students to challenge orthodox views and embrace progressive ideals.
 
• Despite his early death at the age of 22 in 1831, his ideas had a lasting impact on Indian society.
 
 
 
• **French Revolution Influence:**
 
 
• The Young Bengal Movement drew inspiration from the **ideals of the French Revolution**, including liberty, equality, and fraternity.
 
• These principles were applied to challenge traditional social hierarchies and foster intellectual freedom.

questions.question: Sir Michael O’ Dwyer was the Lieutenant Governor of Punjab when the Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred in Amritsar in 1919. Who among the following killed him after 21 years of the incident?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sardar Udham Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• Sardar Udham Singh was an Indian revolutionary who assassinated Sir Michael O’Dwyer on **13 March 1940** in London.
 
• The assassination was carried out as an act of revenge for the **Jallianwala Bagh massacre** that occurred in Amritsar in **1919**.
 
• Sir Michael O’Dwyer was the Lieutenant Governor of Punjab at the time of the massacre, where British troops killed hundreds of unarmed civilians.
 
• Udham Singh was arrested immediately after the assassination and later hanged on **31 July 1940** at Pentonville Prison in London.
 
• Sardar Udham Singh is regarded as a martyr and a symbol of India's struggle for independence.

questions.question: The word 'Green' in Green Revolution refers to ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Crops**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The main objective of the Green Revolution was to increase agricultural production, especially in food crops.
 
• The word 'Green' signifies the greening of crops and development of the agricultural sector.
 
• This revolution started in India in the 1960s under the leadership of Norman Borlaug.
 
• The Green Revolution drastically increased the production of wheat and rice in India.
 
• It helped make India self-sufficient in food grain production.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Components of Green Revolution​:**

 
 
• Improved seeds: Use of high productivity hybrid seeds.
 
• Chemical fertilizers: Extensive use of fertilizers to increase crop production.
 
• Irrigation: Improvement in irrigation facilities and efficient use of water.
 
• Mechanization: Use of agricultural implements and tractors.
 
 
 
• Norman Borlaug: Considered the father of the Green Revolution, who contributed to the development of improved varieties.
 
• Effects of the Green Revolution:
 
 
• Increase in food grain production.
 
• Reduction in poverty and hunger.
 
• Economic improvement in the agricultural sector.
 
 
 
• Challenges**:**
 
 
• Decline in soil fertility.
 
• Excessive water consumption and water crisis.
 
• Ignoring small farmers.

questions.question: Which of the following countries introduced world's first dual-mode vehicle that can run on roads and tracks?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Japan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Japan introduced the world’s first dual-mode vehicle (DMV) that can run on both roads and railway tracks in December 2021.
 
• The DMV, developed by the Asa Seaside Railway Corporation, operates in the Shikoku region of Japan, specifically in Tokushima Prefecture.
 
• This vehicle can switch between road and track modes within 15 seconds, making it highly versatile for transportation.
 
• The DMV is powered by diesel and has a capacity to carry up to 23 passengers.
 
• It is designed to improve connectivity in rural areas where access to railways and roads may be limited.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dual-Mode Vehicle (DMV):**

 
 
• A DMV is a hybrid transport system that can operate on both roads and railway tracks, offering seamless multimodal transportation.
 
• These vehicles are equipped with retractable steel wheels for rail tracks and rubber tires for road surfaces.
 
• DMVs are designed to address connectivity challenges, especially in areas with limited infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Shikoku Region:**
 
 
• Shikoku is one of Japan’s four main islands, known for its rural landscapes and smaller population compared to other regions.
 
• The DMV initiative is aimed at enhancing transportation options in this area to support local communities and tourism.
 
 
 
• **Asa Seaside Railway Corporation:**
 
 
• This regional railway company spearheaded the development of the DMV in Japan.
 
• It operates in Tokushima Prefecture and focuses on innovative solutions to improve mobility in rural areas.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• While Japan is the first to introduce a DMV, similar concepts are being explored globally to enhance transportation efficiency.
 
• Such systems are particularly useful in regions with mixed terrain and limited infrastructure development.

questions.question: The ‘e-Amrit’ project launched by the Government of India in November 2021 is related to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electric Vehicles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **e-Amrit** is a web portal launched by the Government of India in November 2021 to promote the adoption of **electric vehicles (EVs)** in the country.
 
• The portal was developed by **NITI Aayog** in collaboration with the UK Government under the **India-UK Joint Roadmap 2030.**
 
• e-Amrit serves as a one-stop platform for all information related to electric vehicles, including **benefits, policies, subsidies, and incentives.**
 
• The initiative is part of India’s commitment to achieve **net-zero carbon emissions by 2070** and reduce dependence on fossil fuels.
 
• The portal also aims to create awareness about the **economic and environmental advantages** of adopting electric vehicles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electric Vehicles (EVs):**

 
 
• EVs are powered by electricity stored in batteries, eliminating the need for traditional internal combustion engines fueled by petrol or diesel.
 
• They significantly reduce **greenhouse gas emissions** and contribute to cleaner air quality.
 
• EVs come in various types, including **Battery Electric Vehicles (BEVs)** and **Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicles (PHEVs).**
 
• Key components of EVs include electric motors, battery packs, and regenerative braking systems.
 
 
 
• **FAME India Scheme:**
 
 
• Launched by the Government of India to promote Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of Hybrid and Electric Vehicles.
 
• Phase II of the scheme provides financial support for EV adoption and charging infrastructure development.
 
• The scheme aims to reduce dependency on fossil fuels and mitigate air pollution.
 
 
 
• **Battery Technology:**
 
 
• EVs primarily use **lithium-ion batteries**, which are known for high energy density and long life cycles.
 
• Advancements in **solid-state batteries** and recycling technology are crucial for sustainable EV growth.
 
 
 
• **Global EV Trends:**
 
 
• Countries like Norway, China, and the US have made significant strides in EV adoption, supported by policies and infrastructure.
 
• Automakers worldwide are increasingly investing in EV production to align with global carbon-neutral goals.

questions.question: In which of the following places in India, the day temperature rises to 50° Celsius and drops down to near 15° Celsius the same night?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thar Desert**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Thar Desert, also known as the Great Indian Desert, experiences extreme temperature variations due to its arid climate.
 
• Day temperatures in the Thar Desert can rise to as high as 50°C during summer, while nighttime temperatures can drop to near 15°C due to rapid heat loss.
 
• The desert’s sandy terrain has low heat retention capacity, causing significant temperature fluctuations between day and night.
 
• This extreme temperature variation is a characteristic feature of arid and semi-arid regions like the Thar Desert.
 
• The Thar Desert spans Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, and Haryana in India, and also extends into Pakistan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arid Climate:**

 
 
• Characterized by low annual rainfall, high evaporation rates, and extreme temperature fluctuations.
 
• Arid regions often experience very hot days and cool nights due to limited vegetation and moisture.
 
 
 
• **Heat Retention in Sand:**
 
 
• Sand has low heat retention capacity, meaning it heats up quickly during the day and cools rapidly at night.
 
• This property contributes to drastic temperature changes in desert areas.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Life in the Thar Desert:**
 
 
• Extreme temperatures make survival challenging for humans, animals, and plants.
 
• Flora and fauna in the region have adapted to these conditions, such as camels and drought-resistant plants.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Importance:**
 
 
• The Thar Desert is the most densely populated desert in the world, with settlements relying on groundwater and scarce rainfall.
 
• It plays a significant role in India's cultural and economic activities, including tourism and mineral extraction.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT include high powered money?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Post office savings**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **High powered money** refers to the total liability of the monetary authority, which includes the currency held by the public, cash reserves of banks, and other deposits with the RBI.
 
• Post office savings are not included in high powered money as they are not liabilities of the central bank or part of the monetary base.
 
• High powered money plays a crucial role in determining the money supply in the economy through the money multiplier effect.
 
• Components of high powered money include: **currency in circulation, bankers' deposits with the RBI, and other deposits of the RBI.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **High Powered Money (Reserve Money):**

 
 
• It is also known as "monetary base" or "reserve money."
 
• It is created by the central bank (RBI in India) and is the foundation for the money supply in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Components of High Powered Money:**
 
 
• Currency in circulation: Notes and coins held by the public.
 
• Bankers' deposits with the RBI: Reserves held by commercial banks with the central bank.
 
• Other deposits of the RBI: Deposits held by government and financial institutions with the RBI.
 
 
 
• **Post Office Savings:**
 
 
• These include savings accounts and fixed deposits maintained with post offices under various government schemes.
 
• They are not considered part of high powered money as they are not liabilities of the central bank.
 
 
 
• **Money Multiplier Effect:**
 
 
• The process by which the banking system creates money supply based on the reserve base provided by high powered money.
 
• A higher money multiplier indicates greater efficiency in the banking system to create money.

questions.question: Law of giving effect to fundamental rights can only be made by the ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parliament**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In India, the power to enact laws for giving effect to fundamental rights resides with the **Parliament under Article 35 of the Constitution**.
 
• Article 35 specifies that only Parliament can make laws to enforce certain provisions in Part III (Fundamental Rights) of the Constitution.
 
• This provision ensures **uniformity in laws related to fundamental rights across the country**, preventing variations among states.
 
• For example, laws related to punitive measures for offenses under Article 17 (Abolition of Untouchability) or Article 23 (Prohibition of Traffic in Human Beings and Forced Labour) are made exclusively by the Parliament.
 
• The intent of reserving this power for Parliament is to safeguard the supremacy of the Constitution and the integrity of fundamental rights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights**

 
 
• These are a set of rights enshrined in Part III of the Constitution, ensuring equality, freedom, and justice for all citizens.
 
• The six categories of fundamental rights include Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.
 
• They are enforceable by courts, and citizens can approach the judiciary for violations under Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies).
 
 
 
• **Article 35: Key Features**
 
 
• Article 35 empowers only the Parliament to make laws for implementing certain Fundamental Rights, such as laws against untouchability and human trafficking.
 
• It also restricts state legislatures from creating laws on specific matters related to fundamental rights.
 
 
 
• **Role of Judiciary**
 
 
• The judiciary, particularly the Supreme Court, plays a critical role in safeguarding fundamental rights by interpreting laws and striking down unconstitutional provisions.
 
• However, it does not have the legislative power to enact laws—it can only adjudicate upon them.
 
 
 
• **Parliamentary Supremacy in Law-Making**
 
 
• Parliament is the supreme legislative body in India, with the power to make laws for the entire country under the Union List and Concurrent List of the Seventh Schedule.
 
• Its role in enforcing fundamental rights underscores its central position in the democratic framework.

questions.question: Kailasanathar Temple is located in which of the following states of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Kailasanathar Temple is located in **Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu**, India.
 
• It was built during the **Pallava dynasty** by King Narasimhavarman II, also known as Rajasimha, in the 8th century CE.
 
• The temple is dedicated to **Lord Shiva** and is one of the oldest surviving temples in Tamil Nadu.
 
• The architecture of the temple is a classic example of **Dravidian style**, featuring intricate carvings and sculptures.
 
• The Kailasanathar Temple is renowned for its **sandstone construction** and is a significant monument reflecting early South Indian temple architecture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dravidian Architecture**

 
 
• It is a distinct architectural style that originated in South India and is characterized by pyramid-shaped towers called **vimanas**.
 
• Key features include intricately carved pillars, gopurams (gateway towers), and stone sculptures depicting Hindu deities.
 
 
 
• **Kanchipuram**
 
 
• Kanchipuram, also known as the "City of Thousand Temples," is one of the seven sacred cities in Hinduism.
 
• The city is famous for its ancient temples and hand-woven silk sarees.
 
 
 
• **Pallava Dynasty**
 
 
• The Pallavas ruled parts of South India from the 4th to 9th centuries CE.
 
• They were great patrons of art and architecture, contributing significantly to the development of temple architecture.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Lord Shiva Temples**
 
 
• Lord Shiva temples are considered vital in Hinduism as Shiva is one of the principal deities of the religion.
 
• These temples often include a **lingam**, a symbolic representation of Shiva, as the main deity.

questions.question: Which Indian political leader was awarded with Bhutan’s highest civilian honour called the Order of the Druk Gyalpo in December 2021?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Narendra Modi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In December 2021, **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** was conferred with Bhutan’s highest civilian honor, **the Order of the Druk Gyalpo**.
 
• The honor was announced by Bhutan's King **Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck** in recognition of PM Modi’s support and contributions to strengthening India-Bhutan ties.
 
• PM Modi’s leadership in fostering close bilateral relations and cooperation between India and Bhutan during the COVID-19 pandemic was specifically lauded.
 
• The Order of the Druk Gyalpo is a rare and prestigious honor given to individuals who significantly contribute to Bhutan’s welfare and international relations.
 
• PM Modi expressed his gratitude and reaffirmed India’s commitment to its relationship with Bhutan, a trusted neighbor and ally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **India-Bhutan Relations:**

 
 
• India and Bhutan share strong bilateral ties based on mutual trust, cultural similarities, and economic cooperation.
 
• India is Bhutan’s largest trading partner and supports Bhutan in areas like hydropower development, education, and healthcare.
 
• The friendship treaty signed in 1949 was revised in 2007 to reflect mutual sovereignty and independence.
 
 
 
• **Order of the Druk Gyalpo:**
 
 
• It is Bhutan’s highest civilian honor, reserved for individuals who have made exceptional contributions to the nation.
 
• The award symbolizes Bhutan’s gratitude and recognition of remarkable leadership or service.
 
 
 
• **COVID-19 Cooperation:**
 
 
• India supplied COVID-19 vaccines to Bhutan under its Vaccine Maitri initiative, strengthening regional solidarity.
 
• Bhutan praised India’s assistance during the pandemic, including medical supplies and expertise.
 
 
 
• **Bhutan’s Monarchy:**
 
 
• Bhutan is governed by a constitutional monarchy led by King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck.
 
• The monarchy plays a significant role in Bhutan’s development and international relations.

questions.question: Mehtab Bagh is the part of the which of the following famous monuments of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Taj Mahal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mehtab Bagh** is a garden complex situated on the northern side of the Yamuna River, directly opposite the Taj Mahal in Agra, Uttar Pradesh.
 
• It was commissioned by **Mughal Emperor Babur** as one of the last Mughal gardens of his reign.
 
• Mehtab Bagh is perfectly aligned with the Taj Mahal, offering stunning views of the monument, particularly during moonlit nights.
 
• This garden was initially designed as a part of the larger Taj Mahal complex to enhance its aesthetic appeal.
 
• The garden was constructed using traditional Persian-style architecture, a hallmark of Mughal landscaping.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Taj Mahal:**

 
 
• The Taj Mahal, located in Agra, was commissioned by Emperor Shah Jahan in 1632 to house the tomb of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
 
• It is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is considered one of the Seven Wonders of the World.
 
• The structure is built primarily with white marble and features intricate inlay work using semi-precious stones.
 
• The Taj Mahal complex includes a mosque, guesthouse, and several Mughal gardens, such as Mehtab Bagh.
 
 
 
• **Mughal Gardens:**
 
 
• Mughal gardens are characterized by symmetry, flowing water, and geometric patterns inspired by Persian architecture.
 
• Examples include Shalimar Bagh in Kashmir, Nishat Bagh, and the gardens surrounding Humayun’s Tomb.
 
• These gardens often feature raised platforms, pavilions, fountains, and lush greenery.
 
 
 
• **Persian-style Architecture:**
 
 
• Persian architecture heavily influenced Mughal structures, emphasizing symmetry, intricate carvings, and water channels.
 
• Gardens in Persian architecture represent paradise, with flowing water and lush greenery symbolizing eternal life.
 
 
 
• **Agra:**
 
 
• Agra is known for its historical monuments, including the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, and Fatehpur Sikri.
 
• The city served as a capital during the reign of the Mughal Empire.
